messages:
Ellen Park: FYI Guardian Bank escalated to their CTO. Primary blockers: HSM requirement for key custody, strict egress controls (no public endpoints), and they want a signed attestation for pen test results. Need a one-page exec summary + answers by tomorrow noon.
Samir Desai: Oof. Which of those are new vs already in our Private offering?
Ellen Park: HSM is new for them; they specifically asked for FIPS 140-2 Level 3. Egress=no public IPs for inference endpoints. Pen test attestation—they want either our latest 3rd-party report or a commitment timeline.
Tess Nguyen: Quick answers from Sec: we support customer-managed keys in Private via KMS binding in their cloud account. We do not currently offer HSM L3 in hosted. For Dedicated/Private we can discuss HSM appliances in on-prem or FIPS HSM in customer's VPC via partner HSM (requires infra lead).
Ben Ortiz: For the no-public-endpoint ask, we can expose endpoints through a private VPC endpoint and NAT with strict egress. Will need ENG infra ticket to deploy in their account or establish VPN.
Samir Desai: I can sketch the network options. Two patterns: 1) Deploy Redwood Private in their VPC (no public egress), 2) Dedicated in our infra but with customer-controlled egress via proxy endpoint in their cloud. Option 1 is fastest to satisfy residency.
marketing-bot: Reminder: sales exec template updated in /internal/templates/sales-exec-brief.md
Ellen Park: They want a hard yes/no on HSM L3 for the exec sync. If we can't commit, they'll ask the CTO to sign off on a timeline and interim compensating controls.
Tess Nguyen: We should not promise full L3 without engineering buy-in. Proposal: commit to a validated integration plan + timeline (4-6 weeks) for HSM-backed KMS in customer's environment, and in the interim provide enhanced key separation + strict audit logging as compensating control. I can draft the security slide and controls.
Samir Desai: Can we quantify the impact on latency/cost if we route keys to an external HSM? Need at least a ballpark for the CTO.
Ben Ortiz: Latency depends on HSM network hops. For a VPC-deployed HSM in the same region expect ~5-15ms per key op; impact on token generation is minimal if we cache symmetric DEKs. Cost uplift estimate: add roughly 20-30% infra premium for managed HSM or a one-time setup for on-prem.
Ellen Park: Legal asked whether we can produce signed audit logs with tamper evidence. Is that something we can provide from Private installs?
Tess Nguyen: Yes, for Private we can configure forwarders to their SIEM and ship tamper-evident append-only logs (via signed ledger or cloud KMS seals). I'll confirm the exact artifact we can produce.
Samir Desai: Need a short snippet for their firewall team. Minimal allowed list for Guardian sandbox (if they accept our Dedicated endpoint):
```
TCP OUT 10.11.12.34/32 443
TCP OUT 10.11.12.35/32 443
```
If they require no public IPs we'd instead put everything inside their VPC and expose through private endpoints.
Ben Ortiz: Action owners: Tess -> security slide + attestation plan; Samir -> network patterns + latency/cost bullets; Ellen -> exec brief and scheduling; I'll draft the POC SOW language to include HSM timeline and acceptance criteria.
Ellen Park: Also we need to tell them about our pen test cadence. Do we have an up-to-date report we can share under NDA?
Tess Nguyen: We have a 3rd-party pentest (Q4 last year) and a SOC2 Type II report. Both available under NDA. If the CTO insists on a fresh pentest, propose an on-demand pen test at customer's cost or schedule one as part of the onboarding. I'll note that.
Samir Desai: Please note provisioning time: private VPC deployment into customer's account typically 48-72 hours after infra ticket + creds. HSM procurement/integration is separate (4-6 weeks).
marketing-bot: Template hint: include one-line "ask" for execs: approval for POC in customer VPC + sign-off for KMS binding.
Ellen Park: Draft exec slide ask for review: "Request: Approve 6-week POC in Guardian's VPC with customer-managed KMS (HSM integration plan proposed; initial controls available immediately)." Thoughts?
Ben Ortiz: Fine. Add acceptance criteria: successful SAML SSO + sample audit export + bench run showing <100ms avg latency for 2k-token prompts.
Tess Nguyen: I'll add evidence: sample sanitized audit export + stamping mechanism + timeline for HSM delivery.
Samir Desai: I'll attach a simple demo plan for the CTO call: 1) Architecture walkthrough 2) Audit log demo 3) HSM plan & timeline 4) Pricing placeholder.
Ellen Park: Pricing placeholder: don't commit. Offer a provisional POC credit and say commercial terms will follow technical approval.
Ben Ortiz: Filing infra ticket INF-7213 to track VPC deployment.
Tess Nguyen: Filing security ticket SEC-4990 to track HSM decision and pen test docs.
Ellen Park: Great work. Let's aim to have the one-pager + slides and artifacts by 11am tomorrow so I can run with the exec scheduling.
Samir Desai: A couple quick asks: who will be on the CTO call? I can present the network/latency piece.
Ellen Park: I'll invite you, Tess, and Ben. Thanks everyone.
Ellen Park: last_message_ts set to 1850023500 per thread.
